Hi, everyone:

Turns out pyhere doesn't currently recognize the pyproject.toml file as the root of a project's working directly. I upvoted the relevant issue on GitHub. We can use the pyprojroot library instead:

1. Install pyprojroot via the terminal in your course folder's working directory with `uv add pyprojroot`
2. Import the here() function from the pyprojroot.here module with `from pyprojroot.here import here`
3. Use `here()` to write relative file paths as demonstrated in the slides in class today

Play around with the code provided today. I think you'll find polars and plotnine far more intuitive and consistent than pandas and matplotlib.

I appreciate that this week's material can be challenging. Honestly, nobody likes evaluating assumptions and every real data set, as you've discovered, deviates in some way from the ideal. Please know that it's fine -- we're going to do the best we can and be transparent with what we do to address assumption violations. No data perfectly meets all assumptions.

Additional announcements attached.

-Marc
